A hash map is a data structure that stores key-value pairs, enabling efficient insertion, deletion, and lookup operations by using a hash function to compute an index into an array of buckets, where each bucket holds the associated value. This allows for average-case constant-time (O(1)) access to elements, though collisions—when different keys hash to the same index—may require additional handling, such as chaining or open addressing, to maintain performance.
